source_text.body:
Research open-source UI frameworks with sub-agents
User asked Claude Code to research frameworks for an AI-assembled UI feature; it spawned 339 sub-agents in about 10 minutes and used up the five-hour quota.
·
Jun 18, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
The poster asked Claude Code to research open-source frameworks for AI-assembled UI components. Claude started with two general-purpose agents, and because that agent type can use the Agent tool, they recursively spawned more agents up to the product’s nesting limits; afterward, the user checked the transcripts and added a PreToolUse hook to block general-purpose spawns while still allowing safer agent types like Explore and Plan.
How it went
In about 10 minutes it created 339 sub-agent transcript files, and the full turn ran 26 minutes 25 seconds. But 295 of 339 agents hit rate limits and returned nothing, exhausting the MAX 5-hour quota with little useful output.
Worth knowing
The main catch is that general-purpose is the default agent type and there was no built-in confirmation, token-budget warning, or setting to turn off nested spawning.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Research open-source [UI frameworks/libraries] for [feature I want to build]. Use sub-agents, but cap them at [number] so you don't use up my quota. Finish with a comparison table covering maturity, licensing, fit for [my requirement], and a recommendation with reasons.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1u5d02w/til_claude_code_spawned_339_subagents_from_a
